verdict.rationale: GoDaddy documents programmatic registration: a register guide, a quote-token flow for purchase, and a 5-step end-to-end workflow with curl/Node/Python/Go. Its Domains API also lists updating WHOIS contacts, and the v1 spec covers contacts and hosts, so the core is scriptable. Setting nameservers is not explicitly documented: the DNS docs cover records on GoDaddy's own nameservers, and contacts appear only as an update operation. missing for 10: explicit documented nameserver-setting call, contacts supplied as part of the registration request, independent hands-on corroboration of the full scripted flow

support.subject: As a developer, I can register a domain end to end via the API — purchase, contacts, and nameservers in documented calls, so registration can be part of a deploy script

citations.quote: This guide covers registering a domain programmatically using the GoDaddy Domains API.

Every commercial mutation (register,
renew, transfer) requires a `quoteToken` minted by the corresponding quote
collection endpoint.
End-to-end workflow — 5-step transactional flow with curl + Node + Python + Go
API for managing domains, contacts, hosts, and related operations
